content.title: About
content.content: Imitation crab meat (often called crab sticks) is a processed seafood product made primarily from white fish such as pollock, combined with flavorings, colorants, and crab‑like seasoning. It has a mild, slightly sweet taste and a firm, fibrous texture that mimics real crab meat.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The first commercial crab‑like product was created in Japan in the 1970s and called “kani kamaboko”.
The characteristic crab flavor is achieved with a blend of sea salt, sugar, natural crab extracts and artificial flavorings.
The pink hue comes from food‑grade colorants such as carmine or annatto.
It is a staple in sushi, salads and snack dishes because of its low cost and long shelf life.
Imitation crab contains less cholesterol than real crab but can be high in sodium.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Compared with real crab, imitation versions usually have less total fat, making them suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Source of protein
items.content: Provides a moderate amount of animal‑derived protein that supports muscle maintenance.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains B12 and B6, which are important for red blood cell formation and nervous system health.

items.title: Contains essential minerals
items.content: Provides iodine, selenium and zinc, nutrients important for thyroid function and immunity.

items.title: Low calorie
items.content: A 100 g serving typically supplies about 95 kcal, making it a convenient option for calorie‑controlled meals.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: To enhance flavor, the product often contains a lot of salt, which can be problematic for people with hypertension.

items.title: Fish and shellfish allergy
items.content: Since it is made from fish, it can trigger allergic reactions in individuals sensitive to seafood.

items.title: Additives and colorants
items.content: Artificial flavorings and food colorings may not be suitable for everyone.

items.title: Contains MSG
items.content: Some varieties include monosodium glutamate, which can cause headaches in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Imitation crab is used in sushi rolls, salads, pasta dishes, soups and appetizers. Before use, it is usually sliced into strips or cubes. A quick sauté in a little oil can enhance its flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep the unopened package in the refrigerator at 0 °C–4 °C. After opening, transfer to an airtight container and consume within 3–5 days. It can be frozen for up to 2 months, though the texture may change.
